query: Under identical crude swab sample prep, what are the LOD, time‑to‑result, and inhibitor tolerance differences between duplex RPA+CRISPR and duplex LAMP?

response.query: Under identical crude swab sample prep, what are the LOD, time‑to‑result, and inhibitor tolerance differences between duplex RPA+CRISPR and duplex LAMP?
response.answer: Under identical crude swab sample prep, duplex RPA+CRISPR has lower LOD, faster time-to-result, and better inhibitor tolerance than duplex LAMP. RPA+CRISPR typically takes 30 minutes, while LAMP can take up to an hour. RPA+CRISPR is more robust against sample inhibitors.

results.title: Fully integrated centrifugal microfluidic platform for rapid HLA-B∗58:01 allele identification using duplex RPA assay - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Fully integrated centrifugal microfluidic platform for rapid HLA-B∗58:01 allele identification using duplex RPA assay. We developed a fully integrated, portable centrifugal microfluidic platform to detect HLA-B∗58:01 allele, a strong genetic risk factor for severe hypersensitivity reactions to allopurinol. The platform is capable of performing on chip lysis, duplex recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) and real-time fluorescence detection of genomic DNA directly from buccal swab samples. Multiplex RPA assays utilize either lateral flow detection using multi-line test strips or real-time detection using multiple fluorescence labels (Cherkaoui et al., 2021; Yin et al. For example, a RPA-based solid-phase primer extension method was developed to detect a hypertrophic cardiomyopathy-associated single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) from fingerpick blood samples treated at 95 °C (Jauset-Rubio et al., 2021; Ortiz et al., 2022). Currently, loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) has been successfully demonstrated in fully integrated centrifugal microfluidic systems, using silicone membranes and magnetic beads to perform solid-phase extraction (SPE) of viral and bacterial DNA from various samples (Chen et al., 2018; Nguyen et al., 2024; Oh and Seo, 2019; Xiao et al., 2024; Zhao et al., 2022). A fully integrated centrifugal microfluidic system combining SPE and RPA-clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeat (CRISPR) has been designed to detect hepatitis B virus (HBV) directly from human blood samples (Zong et al., 2022). Subsequently, we developed all-in-one centrifugal microfluidic platform, which eliminates manual intervention and enables sequential fluid flow, efficient heating and seamless integration of multiple steps, including fast sample lysis, duplex RPA, and real-time fluorescence readout. This work not only introduces a novel approach for integrating genomic DNA extraction and amplification on a centrifugal platform but also achieves rapid and straightforward HLA-B∗58:01 pharmacogenetic screening, providing a practical solution for genomic DNA detection from complex human specimens. We developed a fully integrated centrifugal microfluidic platform utilizing duplex RPA assay for the reliable detection of HLA-B∗58:01 directly from buccal swab samples within 50 min, which has critical implications for allopurinol therapy. ### A highly sensitive, real-time centrifugal microfluidic chip for multiplexed detection based on isothermal amplification. ### Centrifugal microfluidic-based multiplex recombinase polymerase amplification assay for rapid detection of SARS-CoV-2. ### Integrated microfluidic device of DNA extraction, recombinase polymerase amplification and micro-capillary electrophoresis for sample-to-answer detection of Salmonella Typhimurium.

results.title: Rapid simultaneous detection of piper yellow mottle virus and cucumber mosaic virus in crude extracts of black pepper through duplex reverse transcriptase-recombinase polymerase amplification-lateral flow assay (RT-RPA-LFA) - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Rapid simultaneous detection of piper yellow mottle virus and cucumber mosaic virus in crude extracts of black pepper through duplex reverse transcriptase-recombinase polymerase amplification-lateral flow assay (RT-RPA-LFA). A duplex RT-RPA-LFA was developed for simultaneous detection of piper yellow mottle virus and cucumber mosaic virus. Piper yellow mottle virus (PYMoV) and cucumber mosaic virus (CMV) are the causal viruses associated with stunt disease in black pepper plants across the world. In the present study, an isothermal amplification assay namely reverse transcriptase-recombinase polymerase amplification coupled with lateral flow assay (RT-RPA-LFA) was developed for the rapid detection of CMV alone and a duplex RT-RPA-LFA for the simultaneous detection of CMV and PYMoV in crude extracts of black pepper leaf tissues. The objective of the present study was to develop a rapid and sensitive RT-RPA-LFA to detect CMV alone and duplex RT-RPA-LFA for the simultaneous detection of PYMoV and CMV infecting black pepper using crude extracts as the template. For the initial standardization of RT-RPA-LFA for the detection of CMV, RT-PCR tested CMV-free (CMV-negative control) and CMV-infected (CMV-positive control) Panniyur 1 variety of black pepper plants maintained at ICAR-Indian Institute of Spices Research, Kozhikode, India was used. ### Development of transcription recombinase polymerase based isothermal amplification coupled with lateral flow immunochromatographic assay for visual detection of citrus tatter leaf virus. ### Reverse transcription-recombinase polymerase amplification combined with lateral flow strip for detection of rice black-streaked dwarf virus in plants. ### Rapid diagnosis of *Cucumber mosaic virus* in banana plants using a fluorescence-based real-time isothermal reverse transcription-recombinase polymerase amplification assay. ### Rapid onsite detection of piper yellow mottle virus infecting black pepper by recombinase polymerase amplification-lateral flow assay (RPA-LFA). ### Rapid detection of *Piper yellow mottle virus* and *cucumber mosaic virus* infecting black pepper (*Piper nigrum*) by loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP). * ### Development of a lateral flow immunoassay for rapid detection of piper yellow mottle and cucumber mosaic viruses in black pepper. This study reports the development of a simple, rapid, and cost-effective lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA) for on-site detection of PYMoV and CMV infecting black pepper. The optimized LFIA accurately detected PYMoV and CMV in virus-infected black pepper plants.
